title: Warcry
wikitext:
[[File:Enduring Cry skill screenshot.jpg|thumbnail|right|A player using [[Enduring Cry]]]] '''Warcries''' are a type of [[skill]]s that provide situational benefits to players while also [[taunt]]ing nearby enemies. Most warcries share the behaviour of [[buff]]ing the user and [[nearby]] [[allies]] while also [[exerting]] a number of subsequent attacks, enhancing those attacks with additional properties. ==Mechanics== Warcries are not [[attack]]s or [[spell]]s. Accordingly, they cannot be [[support gem|supported]] by gems limited to attacks or spells, and do not benefit from stats like attack or cast speed. They have their own relevant modifiers, such as {{c|mod|#% increased Warcry Speed}}, in addition to benefitting from generic modifiers to e.g. [[cooldown]] recovery or [[area of effect]]. Players and [[nearby]] [[allies]] can be affected by multiple warcries at once, and multiple warcries can [[exert]] the same attack. Different Warcries normally do not share a cooldown. Warcries have a base radius of 6m. ===Power=== {{main|Power}} Warcries are enhanced proportionately to the power of nearby enemies, calculated at the time they are used. Normal monsters count as 1 power, magic monsters as 2, rare as 10, unique as 20, and players as 5. The following warcries count power differently: * {{il|Rallying Cry}} gains power based on nearby [[Ally|allies]] and enemies * {{il|General's Cry}} gains power based on nearby enemies and enemy [[corpse]]s ===Triggered warcry interactions=== [[Trigger]]ing a warcry (e.g. via {{il|Autoexertion}} or {{il|The Eternal Apple}}): * does not count as using a warcry for "when you use a Warcry" * does count as warcrying for "when you Warcry" * does count as having warcried recently for "If you've Warcried Recently" * does count as having warcried recently for "for each time you've Warcried items.description LIKE "%warcr%" |large=1 |description=1 }} ==Version history== {{Version history table header}} {{Version history table row|3.24.0| * Triggered warcries now count towards "...for each time you've Warcried Recently" stats.{{Undocumented}}Tested in the [[Prohibited Library (community)|Prohibited Library]]. https://discord.com/channels/991073626721763429/991092346651287623/1220888002663022612
https://discord.com/channels/991073626721763429/991092346651287623/1223614765557874729 }} {{Version history table row|3.11.0| * The visual effects of all warcries have been improved. * Greater support for Warcries has been added to the [[Passive Skill|Passive Skill Tree]] in the form of new and changed clusters, and even a [[Call to Arms|new keystone]]. * Warcries no longer share a [[cooldown]] by default. All Warcries now have a base use time of 0.8sec, and their effects tend to linger for a greater [[duration]]. Their base [[cooldown]]s are also now longer. * Each Warcry is enhanced by the proximity of enemies, and for some warcries, [[Ally|allies]] or [[Kill#Corpses|corpses]] too. This is measured as 'Power', with Normal enemies providing 1 Power, Magic enemies providing 2, Rare enemies providing 10, Unique enemies providing 20, and players providing 5. All Warcries also [[taunt]] enemies in range. * Warcries all now cause a certain number of attacks to become [[Exerted]] after the Warcry is used (except {{il|Enduring Cry}} and {{il|General's Cry}}, however the attacks done by the {{il|General's Cry}} [[Mirage Warriors]] are [[Exerted]]). [[Exerted]] attacks are enhanced in different ways depending on the Warcry. Your [[Exerted]] Attacks can benefit from the effects of multiple Warcries, if the type of attack is valid. * We wanted to add support for mechanics that have been added in the past few years that as of yet do not have adequate support on the [[Passive Skill|passive tree]]. Some of these mechanics include [[Rage]], [[Unleash]], [[Corpse|Corpse manipulation]], Warcries, [[Heralds]] and [[Aura#Banners|Banners]]. }} {{Version history table row|2.0.0| * [[Abyssal Cry]] and [[Rallying Cry]] are added to the game. All warcries are now warcries, and shares a cooldown. }} {{Version history table row|0.8.4| * Enduring Cry is introduced to the game, which was a spell. }} {{Version history table end}} ==References== {{reflist}} [[Category:Gem tag mechanics]] [[Category:Gem tags]] {{sister|poe2wiki}}
